resources.string: No network connection. Local servers need Wi-Fi.
The chat experience is served by your Open WebUI instance.
We could not find this server. Check the address, and make sure your phone is on the same network as the server.
The server refused the connection. Check that Open WebUI is running, that it listens on 0.0.0.0, and that your firewall allows the port.
The server took too long to respond. Check your Wi-Fi or mobile network, then try again.
Connect to Wi-Fi or mobile data. For a local server, make sure you are on the same Wi-Fi network as the server.
The HTTPS certificate could not be verified. Expuz AI never ignores certificate errors. Use a valid certificate, or connect over your trusted LAN during development.
The server responded with an error. Try again, or check the Open WebUI logs if it keeps happening.
The server returned an unexpected response. Try again in a moment.
The Android browser engine crashed or ran out of memory. Reload the page to continue. Your login session is kept.
Expuz AI only loads pages from your configured server. Use the button below to review the server address.
Use HTTPS for remote servers. Plain HTTP is only available for private LAN addresses in development builds.
Something went wrong while loading the server. Check your connection and try again.
Expuz AI never bypasses TLS certificate errors or loads unapproved external pages inside the app.
This link goes to %1$s and will open in your browser. Expuz AI stays in the background.
Download started. Check your Downloads folder.
This file type cannot be downloaded inside the app.
Navigation to an unapproved address was blocked.
This server requested native HTTP authentication, which is not supported. Sign in through the web UI instead.
Could not open the Android file picker.
No app can open this link.
HTTP cache cleared. Reloading the frontend.
Expuz AI is a native shell for your own Open WebUI. The chat interface is served by your server, so frontend updates appear without reinstalling the app.
On a phone, localhost means the phone itself. Use your PC LAN address, or a public HTTPS domain.
Your server address stays on this device. The APK contains no API keys or backend credentials.
Later, add separate local and remote addresses in Settings for local-first fallback.
Expuz AI could not reach this server. You can still save the address and try again when the server is available.
Address looks valid. You can connect now.
Enter a valid server address, for example http://192.168.x.x:8080.
Only http:// and https:// addresses are supported.
Do not include a username or password in the URL.
Remove the query string and fragment from the server URL.
Use HTTPS for remote servers. Plain HTTP is only allowed on a private local network.
This build does not allow plain HTTP. Use HTTPS, or install the debug build for LAN development.
Enter a valid host name or IP address.
Enter a valid port between 1 and 65535.
Plain HTTP is blocked by this build
Could not connect to the server
Automatic mode probes the local server first. If it is unavailable, Expuz AI offers the remote server with an explicit confirmation so a login session is never silently lost.
Use one server address. Changing to a different origin may require signing in again; the app asks first.
Only the local address is used. This is ideal when the phone is always on the same Wi-Fi as the server.
Only the remote HTTPS address is used. Recommended when you are away from the local network.
The new address uses a different origin. Cookies and local storage are stored per origin, so you may need to sign in again. The current login is not deleted. Continue?
Add a local server URL for this mode.
Add a remote server URL for this mode.
Add at least one local or remote server URL.
The chat UI is served by your server. Update Open WebUI there, then reload here — no APK rebuild needed.
Reloads the page from the server. Cached files are used when the server allows it.
Forces CSS, JavaScript and images to download again. Cookies and local storage stay intact, so you remain signed in.
Cached frontend files will be downloaded again. Your login session and app settings are kept.
Remote servers must use HTTPS. Certificate errors are never ignored. No API keys or backend credentials are stored in this app.
The active URL is chosen from these addresses.
